1  MFA No. 202380 of 2022 KALABURAGI IN MVC NO. 665/2018 BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT AS PRAYED FOR, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY AND HOLD BOTH THE RESPONDENTS JOINTLY AND SEVERALLY LIABLE TO PAY THE ENHANCED COMPENSATION TO THE APPELLANT.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT

The appellant/claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM at Kalaburagi (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.665/2018 by judgment and award dated 15.07.2021.
2.
The claimant was riding a motorcycle on 09.04.2018 at 11.00 a.m. and met with an accident involving a Tempo-Trax bearing registration No.KA-32/C- 4480.

The claimant suffered injuries and was shifted to Kamareddy Hospital, Kalaburagi and thereafterwards shifted to ASM Hospital,
Kalaburagi for higher treatment.
At the hospital, it was diagnosed that the claimant had suffered contused abrasion over left knee, cut lacerated wound over left elbow and fracture of tibial condyle of left side.

The claimant claimed that he was an agriculturist and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/-
per month and due to the accidental injuries, he was not in a position to carry on any agricultural activity.

3. The claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V.Act') claiming compensation of Rs.25,90,000/- from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The claim petition was opposed by the insurer while the owner of the offending vehicle was placed exparte.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P14.
He also examined the doctor, who treated him as PW.2.
The insurer marked a copy of the policy as Ex.R1.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tempo-Trax.
It held that the claimant was an agriculturist and his notional income was considered at a sum of Rs.11,750/- per month.

It held that the claimant had suffered injuries as found in the wound certificate at Ex.P4 and based on the evidence of PW.2, it held that the claimant has suffered disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body and awarded the following compensation:
1 Towards pain and suffering Rs.30,000/-
2. Towards Medical Expenses Rs.1,06,883/-
3. Towards diet and attendant Rs.40,000/-

Towards loss of amenities Rs.10,000/-
 Total Rs.4,50,083/-
 Rounded off Rs.4,50,000/-
Being aggrieved by the same, the present appeal is filed.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that the claimant was an agriculturist and therefore, the fracture of tibial condyle on the left side affected his daily activities as an agriculturist.

He submitted that PW.2 has categorically deposed before the Court that the claimant had suffered the disability to the extent of 30% and therefore, the Tribunal ought to have considered the effect of the fractures on the activities of the claimant as an agriculturist.
He submits that the disability was permanent and had affected his daily activities and therefore, the Tribunal ought to have considered the disability at 20%.
He further submitted that the Tribunal awarded meager compensation under conventional heads.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2-insurer submits that PW.2 deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 10% to the limb and the as per the ALIMCO guidelines, the disability to the whole body was rightly considered at 10% and the Tribunal was justified in awarding the compensation.
6.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned counsel for respondent No.2.
7. The fact that the claimant was an agriculturist is not seriously disputed.
The fracture of left tibial condyle bone, would invariably leave the appellant partially disabled, if not fully.
Though the evidence of PW.2 suggests that the fracture had united, but yet the claimant may not be in a position to carry on his activities with a weak bone.

In that view of the matter, the disability suffered by the appellant deserves to be enhanced to 15% to the whole body in view of the fact that the disability is permanent in nature, which could affect his functions.

In addition, the Tribunal has awarded a sum Kabir Ali @ Kabir S/O Sultansab Sultan ... vs Hanamantray S/O Tejiray And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153747861/
3 of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering notwithstanding the fact that the claimant had suffered the fracture of a vital bone and other wounds.

sentences.text: In that view of the matter, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering also deserves to be enhanced to a sum of Rs.50,000/-.
Likewise, towards loss of income during laid up period which must have been taken at 3 months and therefore, the compensation under this head also deserves enhancement.
Similarly, loss of amenities is assessed at Rs.10,000/- while the compensation must have been not less than Rs.50,000/-.
8. In that view of the matter, the compensation is re
- determined as follows:

1 Towards pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
2. Towards Medical Expenses Rs.1,06,883/-
3.

Towards diet and attendant Rs.40,000/-
charges 4.

Towards loss of income during Rs.35,250/-
laid up period (11,750x3)
5.

Towards loss of future earning Rs.3,59,550/-
capacity (11,750x12x17x15%)

6. Towards loss of amenities Rs.50,000/-
7.
Towards future medical expenses Rs.15,000/-

In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.4,50,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.6,56,683/-.

The enhanced compensation of Rs.2,06,683/- is payable by respondent No.2 - Insurance Company along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
The insurer is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation and interest before the Tribunal within one month from the date of receipt of of a copy of this order.
Out of the enhanced compensation, 50% of the same and interest shall be deposited in the name of the appellant/claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 is permitted to file his memo of appearance/vakalath within a period two weeks.
